decision.title: Identity-Anchored Reconciliation Cursor (Amendment to ADR-022 Clause 3)
decision.mechanism: Identity-anchored resume: the persisted, bounded (SortName, itemId) Cache record stays; the resume locates the record's boundary item by its unique itemId in the host's own candidate order via clause 3's own bounded-linear-skip-at-run-start branch (no host keyset predicate exists); the unsupported host-predicate seek branch is withdrawn; an unlocatable anchor resets to the start (clause 5).
decision.host_order: SortName ASC, Name ASC (raw item Name, not the item id); no supported OrderBy/ItemSortBy identifier tie-break; the (SortName, Name) order is not a guaranteed strict total order.
decision.resume_bound: One run is bounded by the server-wide candidate count N plus QueueCapacity, with an O(offset) page-reach resume (bounded ReconciliationBatchSize pages, cancellation between and inside pages, yields per clause 7); a full round-robin cycle is O(N^2/QueueCapacity) cumulative skip work. 'Bounded' is not a constant bound.
caveats: Rows tying on the exact (SortName, Name) pair have no host-guaranteed relative order.
The enumerator query is server-wide (N is the server-wide movie+episode candidate count), so a late-cycle resume scans a large prefix every run.
The host order is an internal implementation detail with no plugin compatibility promise.

residual_limitations.description: Per-run resume is O(offset) ordered rows and a full cycle is O(N^2/QueueCapacity) cumulative skip work; N is the server-wide movie+episode candidate count because the enumerator query is not library-scoped.
residual_limitations.register_when: docs/limitations/open.md / architecture when F4 is resolved by task 19.5; recorded in ADR-029 Consequences now.

residual_limitations.description: Rows tying on the exact (SortName, Name) pair have no host-guaranteed relative order, so a page boundary inside such a tie can re-cover or persistently skip an item across a cycle.
residual_limitations.register_when: docs/limitations/open.md / architecture when F4 is resolved by task 19.5; recorded in ADR-029 Consequences now.

residual_limitations.description: Removing or making ineligible the boundary anchor resets the cursor to the start, re-covering one cycle's prefix (a bounded but visible cost).
The host order is an internal implementation detail with no plugin compatibility promise; the mechanism degrades to a rescan/restart, not a wrong result, if it changes.

task_impacts.impact: Now implements the amended clause 3: the persisted bounded (SortName, itemId) Cache cursor whose resume locates the boundary item by its unique itemId in the host's (SortName, Name) order via a bounded linear skip (no host-predicate seek), with reset-to-start when the anchor cannot be located. The bounded enqueue-outcome vocabulary, cursor-advance rule, scope reset, post-save exclusion, and per-run bounds are unchanged.

Now covers the amended resume: successive-run coverage tests must include the identity-anchor resume case (locate-by-itemId, add/remove before the anchor does not shift the resume point, wrap), in addition to the existing coalesce/in-flight/overflow-stop and library-mutation cases (see verification_requirements_for_19_2).
Finalizes the F4 open-limitation resolution and records the registered residual limitations in the canonical limitation/architecture surfaces when the phase lands.

verification_requirements_for_19_2: Identity-anchor resume: with a persisted (SortName, itemId) cursor, a run resumes at the page strictly after the boundary item located by its unique itemId in the host's (SortName, Name) order; the SortName component is a hint/diagnostic, not the ordering authority.
Unlocatable anchor: when the boundary item was removed or became ineligible, the cursor resets to the start and the run does not fail.

Library mutation before the anchor: adding/removing an item before the cursor does not shift the resume point (items after the cursor are covered in the current cycle; items before are covered at the next wrap or after a scope reset).
Successive-run coverage: runs over a scope larger than QueueCapacity cover the whole scope over time (round-robin) and the cursor wraps at the end.
Coalesce case: a Coalesced enqueue is covered and does not stall the run.
In-flight case: an InFlight enqueue is covered and does not stall the run.
Overflow-stop: the run stops at the first Overflow and advances the cursor only over the covered prefix; the next run resumes at the first uncovered item.
Stopped case: a Stopped outcome stops the run the same way.
Scope reset: a changed enabled-library/item-type scope tuple resets the cursor to the start.
Trigger exclusion: event, webhook, per-item, and post-save triggers do not read or write the cursor.

Per-run boundedness honesty: the resume scan is walked in bounded ReconciliationBatchSize pages with cancellation between and inside pages and yields per clause 7; the test asserts the page-reach/offset bound (server-wide candidate count plus QueueCapacity), not a constant bound.

Tie caveat: a test documents (or exercises) that coverage is guaranteed for rows strictly ordered by (SortName, Name) and is best-effort for rows tying on the exact pair; the tie case is a registered residual, not asserted as covered.
